stories.headline: Glacial collapse triggered Nepal flash floods, not earthquake: USGS
stories.title: Glacial collapse triggered Nepal flash floods, not earthquake: USGS
stories.summary: Washington, Aug 27: The Nepal flash floods were triggered by a glacial collapse and not by a 4.4 magnitude earthquake as reported earlier, the US Geological Survey (USGS) said. The USGS said additional analysis of the long-period seismic waves indicated that the tremors were generated by a glacial collapse and debris flow. The flash floods originating in Tibet on Wednesday left a trail of death and destruction in Rasuwa and Dhading districts of Nepal, killing 162 people and leaving 750, including 133 Indian nationals, missing. “This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake. Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred,” the USGS said in an update to its note on the event. It also upgraded the magnitude of the seismic event to 5.2 from the 4.4 assessed earlier. “The USGS determined that the seismic event was a glacial collapse and debris flow that caused subsequent catastrophic impacts downstream,” it said. Daniel Shugar, an Associate Professor of geomorphology at the University of Calgary in Canada said the flash floods were triggered by a glacier that rolled off a cliff at 5,200 meters. Shugar compared the satellite images of the region taken on Wednesday and Tuesday, a day before the natural disaster struck Nepal. “Comparing satellite imagery from yesterday and today, the glaciers in the vicinity do seem to have lost a fair bit of snow in the last 24 hours,” Shugar was quoted as saying by the New Scientist magazine. “My guess is that snow melt, and glacier ice melt as well, injected a lot of liquid water into the glacier, which percolated down to the bed and lubricated it. That was enough for it to collapse,” he said.

stories.headline: Nepal flash flood kills 100, leaves hundreds missing; earthquake-avalanche link under probe
stories.title: Nepal flash flood kills 100, leaves hundreds missing; earthquake-avalanche link under probe
stories.summary: At least 100 people have been killed and hundreds remain missing after a devastating flash flood swept through Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot districts along the Tibet border on Wednesday, with officials warning that the death toll could rise as rescue teams reach cut-off areas. The Nepal Tourism Board (NTB) said 384 travellers were preliminarily reported missing, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepalis. The figures are still being verified, with authorities cross-checking records with travel agencies, guides, local administrations and security agencies. According to The Himalayan Times, at least 105 Indian nationals and 37 non-resident Indians (NRIs) are among those reported missing. The number of Indian nationals could increase as verification continues. The NTB said 59 of the Indian nationals were travelling through Samrat Tours & Travels and 46 through Leaf Holiday, while the 37 NRIs were listed separately under Himalayan Glacier. The preliminary list also includes foreign travellers from the UK, Malaysia, the US and South Africa. The flood struck the Bhote Koshi River at around 8.30 am, sweeping through parts of Rasuwa before affecting the Trishuli River and settlements in Nuwakot. Nepal Police said 114 people have been rescued from the Bhotekoshi River area in Rasuwa, where flash floods struck on Wednesday, according to local media. The Nepal Army rescued more than 80 people by helicopter, while private helicopter companies rescued another 29, Nepal TV and Radio Nepal reported. Earthquake may have triggered avalanche A possible chain of events behind the disaster has emerged, with Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal telling Parliament that preliminary information indicated an earthquake at around 8.37 am triggered an avalanche, which in turn caused the flash floods. Khanal stressed that the information was still being verified. He said China’s Tibet region had also suffered “huge damage” and that Nepal was coordinating with Chinese authorities. The minister said 26 police personnel, nine armed police personnel and 44 military personnel were missing. Customs and immigration officials were also among those unaccounted for. There has been extensive damage to roads, bridges, communication networks and hydropower infrastructure, with Rasuwa and Nuwakot the worst affected districts, Khanal said. Earlier, Nepal’s Department of Hydrology and Meteorology had said the flooding was not caused by heavy rainfall. Less than seven millimetres of rain had been recorded in Rasuwa over the previous 24 hours, prompting authorities to examine other possible causes, including a glacial event. Buildings collapse, bridge swept away The scale of the destruction has emerged through verified videos reviewed by the BBC. Footage from the Trishuli Bazaar area of Nuwakot, about 25 km north-west of Kathmandu, showed the river suddenly swelling with huge volumes of fast-moving, sediment-filled water. A bridge was swept away by the force of the floodwaters, followed moments later by the collapse of several multi-storey buildings. Other footage showed the aftermath, with trees and buildings near the riverbank washed away, partially collapsed or covered in thick layers of mud and debris. The flood also reportedly swept away around 60 houses near Trishuli Bazaar and damaged two motorable bridges. District Police Office chief Bipin Regmi said three unidentified bodies were recovered from the Trishuli River bank in Nuwakot — two at Simchaur and one at Kolputar. At least 17 people have been rescued so far. The Nepal Army said 12 people were evacuated by helicopter — six from Syafrubesi, two from Mailung and four from Dhunche. Four Army and eight private helicopters have been mobilised for search and rescue operations. Security personnel, officials among missing Fourteen employees of the Rasuwa Customs Office in Timure also remain out of contact, including 11 permanent and three contract staff. Twenty-five other employees, including Chief Customs Administrator Rajendra Dhungana, have been accounted for, according to Nepal’s Finance Ministry. The disaster has disrupted roads and bridges, making access to some affected areas difficult. Five people stranded by the flood were rescued and taken to Chakradev Hospital in Bidur, while access to Trishuli Hospital was disrupted after roads and bridges were washed away. The flood also damaged the Trishuli and Devighat hydropower projects and swept away three blocks and a substation of a 25-MW solar power plant. Travellers remain unaccounted for The large number of missing travellers has added a major international dimension to the disaster. The BBC quoted a Chinese businessman based in Kathmandu, Yee Liang, as saying his logistics company had seven container trucks in the affected area, all staffed by Nepali employees. “We have lost contact with all of them. There is no signal, so we cannot reach anyone,” he said. Yee said he was not aware of any warning before the flood. “There were occasional mudslides and landslides, especially in the rainy season, but this one seems much more serious,” he told the BBC. On the Tibetan side, Guan Daoxuan, based in Sichuan province, told the BBC that he had lost contact with his wife, who works for a state-run construction company involved in building roads and bridges in Tibet. Chinese state media have reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a trade hub on the Tibetan side of the border. Chinese President Xi Jinping has called for an “all-out” search for missing people and stronger monitoring and early-warning systems to prevent further disasters. Rescue and relief operations intensified The Nepal government has mobilised the Nepal Police, Armed Police Force, Army and district administrations for search, rescue and relief operations. Prime Minister Balendra Shah has directed government agencies to ensure close coordination, while President Ram Chandra Paudel called on government bodies, political parties, social organisations and citizens to intensify rescue efforts. The World Health Organization is preparing medicines and equipment for around 1,000 people, along with 15 emergency tents. Nepal’s Health Ministry has reserved 100 emergency beds at Bir Hospital and the Trauma Centre in Kathmandu and deployed medical teams to support the operation. With many areas still inaccessible and hundreds of people unaccounted for, officials are continuing to verify casualty and missing-person figures. The death toll is therefore expected to remain provisional until search teams can reach the worst-hit areas. PM Modi speaks to Nepal counterpart, assures all possible assistance Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah following the deadly flash floods in parts of Nepal and assured him of India’s “all possible humanitarian assistance”. PM Modi conveyed his condolences over the loss of lives and said India stood in solidarity with the people of Nepal during the crisis. “Spoke to Prime Minister Balendra Shah and conveyed condolences on the loss of lives due to the floods in Nepal. The people of India stand in solidarity with their sisters and brothers in Nepal at this difficult time,” Modi said in a post on X. He added that India was coordinating “closely on rescue and relief efforts” with Nepal.

stories.headline: India sends second flight with 37.5 tonnes of aid to flood-hit Nepal
stories.title: India sends second flight with 37.5 tonnes of aid to flood-hit Nepal
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 27 : India on Thursday dispatched a second flight carrying 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian supplies, medicines, and food packets to support Nepal's relief efforts after devastating flash floods that have left over 160 dead and hundreds missing. External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar took to X and reaffirmed India's commitment to supporting Nepal in the rescue and relief operations. "A second flight has just taken off, carrying 37.5 tonnes of HADR material, medicines & food packets for Nepal," EAM Jaishankar said in a post on X. "India remains in close and continuous touch with the Nepalese authorities. We will continue to strongly support the ongoing relief efforts," he added. According to the latest official update, the bodies of 162 people swept away by a massive flash flood in Nepal's Bhote Koshi River have been recovered as of Thursday morning. The remains were recovered from riverbanks in several downstream districts along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river systems, including Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu, Nawalparasi (East) and Nawalparasi West, the Police said in a notice. The aid follows a first 10-tonne shipment sent on Wednesday. India's Ambassador to Nepal, Naveen Srivastava, formally handed over the aid consignment to Nepal's Minister of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation, Khadak Raj Paudel. The assistance includes essential relief materials to help communities affected by widespread flooding and landslides. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India stands firmly with Nepal and remains committed to extending all possible support. The floods in Nepal, triggered by heavy monsoon rains, have caused extensive damage to infrastructure, homes and agricultural land, displacing thousands of families. Rescue and relief operations are ongoing across several provinces, with local authorities struggling to cope with the scale of the disaster. India's assistance comes as part of its longstanding policy of 'Neighbourhood First', under which New Delhi has consistently provided humanitarian aid to neighbouring countries during emergencies. --IANS

stories.headline: Assam: Team of boatmen saves over 1,000 lives in devastating Dikhow flood
stories.title: Assam: Team of boatmen saves over 1,000 lives in devastating Dikhow flood
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: NAZIRA: A 27-member team of local boatmen has emerged as a symbol of courage and humanity after risking their own lives to rescue more than 1,000 people during the devastating flood that hit Upper Assam on July 19.
The unprecedented surge in the Dikhow river created a terrifying situation at Bihubar Shiloni under Nazira sub-district of Sivasagar.
Within moments, the normally calm river turned into a raging torrent, with tsunami-like waves sweeping away houses and devastating Bihubar and several neighbouring villages.
Amid desperate cries for help from residents and livestock, many people were forced to take shelter on rooftops and trees to save their lives.

At a time when people were waiting for rescue teams and boats from the SDRF and NDRF, a 27-member local team led by people such as Shravan Prasad, Narayan Choudhury, Rajkumar Rajbhar, and Ravi Rajbhar came forward.
Using their six small boats, the team divided themselves into groups of six or seven and launched rescue operations.
From around 11 am until 1-2 am, they rescued approximately 1,200-1,300 people from Bihubar Shiloni, Nepalikuthi, Mirdhabasti, Signal Basti, Natun Basti, and several other villages.
The rescue operation was extremely dangerous.
Strong currents and huge trees, branches, and bamboo being swept downstream posed a constant threat to the rescuers.
However, the experienced boatmen continued their mission despite the risks and succeeded in saving more than a thousand lives.
The team members reportedly had little food and water during the prolonged rescue operation, but they remained focused on saving those trapped in the floodwaters.
After stopping the operation around 2 am because of darkness and exhaustion, they returned the following morning to resume rescue efforts.

article_sentences: Vigilance has been stepped up in Uttarakhand's border district of Champawat following severe floods in Nepal on Wednesday (August 26, 2026).
The Tanakpur post of the SDRF has been placed on high alert, and people have been urged to stay away from the banks of the Sharda River, officials said.
According to officials, the Tanakpur post in Champawat district has been put on high alert under the instructions of State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) Commandant Arpan Yaduvanshi.
The SDRF's Tanakpur team is continuously monitoring and patrolling vulnerable riverbank areas, including the Sharda Ghat, the Sharda Barrage, and surrounding localities.
The team is keeping a close watch on the river's water level and potential risks while maintaining coordination with the local administration.
Officials said that the SDRF team visited the Sharda Ghat and low-lying areas to alert local residents, travellers and fishermen about the potential rise in the river's water level.
People have been urged not to venture near the riverbanks unnecessarily under any circumstances and to adhere to safety guidelines issued by the administration.
They added that the SDRF team is fully prepared round-the-clock with essential life-saving and rescue equipment to initiate immediate relief and rescue operations in the event of any emergency.
The Uttarakhand government has also issued helpline numbers to assist the state’s people stranded there.
Officials said that the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority (USDMA) has released these helpline numbers to aid the people.

If any person from Uttarakhand is stranded in the affected area of Nepal, or if anyone wishes to share information regarding an individual, they can contact the helpline numbers of the State Emergency Operation Centre (SEOC) in Dehradun.
According to officials, apart from the SEOC numbers—0135-2710334, 2710335, 2664314, 2664315, 2664316, and 8218867005—people can also contact the toll-free number 1070.

article_sentences: A deadly flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa border district has sharpened calls from Hindu Kush Himalaya lawmakers for stronger regional cooperation on climate risks.

At the 2nd HKH Parliamentarians’ Meet in Bhutan, speakers urged collective action, climate-smart laws and investments, and cross-border preparedness to protect vulnerable mountain communities and downstream populations across the eight-country region.

The devastating flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district along the Nepal-China border underscores the urgent need for stronger regional cooperation to address climate risks that transcend national boundaries, parliamentarians from across the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH) region said on August 26, 2026.

The lawmakers were speaking at the 2nd Hindu Kush Himalaya Parliamentarians’ Meet in Thimphu, Bhutan, according to a statement by the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD).

Participants said the disaster highlighted the importance of collective action, stronger preparedness, and sustained regional cooperation to reduce climate-related risks and build resilience across the HKH region.

The two-day meeting, taking place from August 26 to 27, brings together legislators from across the region to exchange experiences, discuss emerging climate risks, and explore how policies, legislation, and public investments can better support adaptation and resilience.
Opening the meeting, Deputy Speaker Sangay Khandu of the National Assembly of Bhutan stressed the role of parliamentarians in turning climate commitments into action.
“Resilience cannot live in scientific reasoning anymore or in the speeches of ministers and government officials or members of parliament.
It cannot live only in the commitments we make at the global stage,” he said.
“Resilience should be carefully woven into the fabric of our laws, our budgets, our institutions and our actions on the ground.
It is parliamentarians who have the power to ensure it.”
Participants highlighted that climate risks are increasingly affecting communities across borders and require coordinated responses that go beyond national efforts.

Later, both Aadhav Arjuna and the Chief Minister had informed the court that they intended to file applications for rejecting the election petitions.

stories.headline: AI can augment reasoning but cannot substitute judicial conscience: CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: AI can augment reasoning but cannot substitute judicial conscience: CJI Surya Kant
stories.summary: New Delhi, Aug 27: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday said the judiciary’s governing principle is that artificial intelligence may augment judicial reasoning, but it cannot substitute judicial conscience, and that a permanent apex body has been proposed to supervise the adoption and accountability of the new technology. Speaking at a bilateral meeting with Ulrich Herrmann, the presiding judge of the Federal Court of Justice at Karlsruhe in Germany, CJI Kant said that artificial intelligence (AI) is being used in certain defined support functions such as legal research, judgement translation into 16 languages and as a conversational interface for citizens to look for case status and procedures. He said that while these tools are designed to reduce repetitive work, they do not determine judicial outcomes. “Artificial intelligence may augment judicial reasoning, but it cannot substitute judicial conscience. Draft regulations from the Supreme Court's AI Committee permit administrative uses such as scheduling, transcription and translation, while barring AI from assessing witness credibility, flight risk, recidivism or bail eligibility; a permanent apex body has been proposed to supervise the adoption and accountability of AI,” he said. “Our two judiciaries share the same underlying responsibility: to preserve judicial independence and public confidence while adapting our institutions to new forms of litigation and new expectations of access. “Technology and administrative reform can support this responsibility, but neither can replace careful adjudication, human judgment and fidelity to law,” he said. The CJI said that institutional mediation centres, Lok Adalats and digital Lok Adalats, including the Supreme Court's recent special Lok Adalat, ‘Samadhan Samaroh’, have brought settlement within reach of parties well beyond major cities, supported by trained professionals, case managers and secure digital systems. “As two major trading partners, our judiciaries and mediation institutions stand to gain from exchanging experience on cross-border commercial mediation, the recognition and enforcement of mediated settlements, and joint training for mediators handling India-Germany commercial disputes,” he said. At the outset, the CJI said that both the countries have developed different judicial structures and legal traditions, as India follows a common-law tradition with one integrated judicial hierarchy, while Germany has a civil-law system with separate branches of federal jurisdiction. “These differences make the exchange particularly useful. They allow us to compare how our institutions deal with the same practical concerns, including appellate workload, consistency of case law, timely disposal, judicial administration and access to justice,” he said. The CJI said he is approaching the meeting with three themes that speak directly to the challenges the two judiciaries share, such as harnessing technology and AI in the administration of justice, strengthening cross-border mediation and other dispute resolution mechanisms, and deepening institutional cooperation through an MoU. “I also see considerable value in identifying areas in which our courts, judges, registries and judicial academies can continue this engagement through a structured and reciprocal programme,” he said. The CJI said he sees value in anchoring any MoU in the themes already discussed: technology and AI in court administration, and cross-border mediation and dispute resolution, alongside the commercial and business law focus and the digitalisation of judicial processes that the Hanseatic court's concept note already identifies as priorities. “I propose that each side identify one institutional point of contact so that today's discussion can be converted into a workable programme, with the MoU or another suitable arrangement to follow once the appropriate authorities on both sides have considered its scope, frequency, participants, confidentiality requirements and working language,” he said. Giving an overview of the Indian judiciary, the CJI said that unlike Germany, India has no separate constitutional court. “The Supreme Court is simultaneously the final appellate court in civil and criminal matters and the country's highest constitutional court, with original jurisdiction under Article 32 to enforce fundamental rights,” he said. The CJI also said that India’s approach has been to make courts not merely more technological, but more accessible, transparent and responsive for every stakeholder in the justice delivery system. On the shared institutional challenge, CJI Kant said Germany's electronic case files, the e-Justice council, the Bund-Laender Commission and the proposed Federal Justice Cloud reflect a similar commitment to a secure digital foundation for justice delivery. “Both our judiciaries agree that judicial decisions must remain with judges and legally authorised judicial officers, whatever the degree of digital transformation,” he said. Promoting mediation as another mode of dispute resolution has always been at the top of the priority list of the Chief Justice of India, right from day one, CJI Kant said. The CJI is on a four-day visit to Germany and the UK during which he will address several programmes.

stories.headline: Japan Struggles To Attract Solar Bids, Lessons For India
stories.title: Japan Struggles To Attract Solar Bids, Lessons For India
stories.summary: A Mature Market Running Out of Easy Sites Japan added 5.8 GW of solar in 2025, a respectable pace for a land-constrained, densely built country, but the most recent auction data suggests the Feed in Premium tariffs (FIP) mechanism itself is straining. Unlike the older feed-in tariff system it replaced, FIP tariffs are explicitly designed to shrink over successive rounds as a maturing market is expected to need less support. The problem is that Japan's remaining greenfield sites are disproportionately the difficult ones, be it mountainous terrain, land-use conflicts, or locations requiring costly grid upgrades. A shrinking premium on top of that is making marginal projects harder to underwrite. Developers appear to be sitting out rounds rather than bidding at tariffs that no longer work out. Recent Auction Seven companies split just a third of the capacity Japan put up for bids in its 29th solar auction, extending a run of undersubscribed rounds that offers some pointers perhaps for India's own auction economics. Japan's power auctioneer awarded just 38.2 MW out of 115 MW put up for bidding, continuing a run of undersubscribed rounds that is starting to look less like an anomaly and more like a pattern in one of the world's most mature solar markets. And one might add, well paying ones. The Organization for Cross-regional Coordination of Transmission Operators (OCCTO) said that of the seven companies that split eight winning bids for projects of at least 250 kW, AC12 took the largest share at 29.9 MW; Sandia, Japan Petroleum Exploration and Solar Field 13 rounded out the rest. The weighted-average winning tariff came in at ¥8.89 (~Rs 5.32)/kWh, just under OCCTO's ceiling price of ¥9.6/kWh. A clear sign that competitive tension in the auction was thin rather than fierce. The shortfall is not new. Of 13 business plans submitted for eligibility screening, only eight bids totalling 38.2 MW were ultimately submitted with some developers who cleared the eligibility bar simply chose not to bid the full amount they qualified for. Japan's 26th auction saw a similar pattern: 163 MW offered, only 75.4 MW awarded to 16 companies, a 46 percent fill rate. The 27th auction produced a lower weighted-average tariff of ¥4.61/kWh on a smaller pool of interest, and the 28th awarded 89.2 MW across 29 bids. Four consecutive rounds, four undersubscribed outcomes. The Indian Contrast And Future Pointers India's own auction experience has run in almost the opposite direction for most of the past decade: SECI and state-level tenders have typically been oversubscribed, with tariffs falling because competition for capacity remained intense even as the ceiling prices themselves were reduced round over round. India added a record 27 GW of solar in the first half of 2026 alone, and the country's tariff discovery process has generally been treated as evidence that aggressive price competition and high participation can coexist. But the conditions that produced Japan's fall-off, namely, a maturing pipeline, shrinking premiums, and constrained sites are not unique to Japan, and India is not immune to the same mechanics showing up later. MNRE Secretary flagged this month that nearly 42 GW of solar capacity is struggling to find offtake buyers, with grid curtailment eating into project economics in the same states that pioneered the low-tariff auction model. If ceiling prices in future Indian rounds are set without enough regard for the deteriorating economics of curtailment-exposed, storage-less capacity, the same undersubscription pattern Japan is now living through is not just a hypothetical risk but a real possibility.

stories.headline: India's Plan To Solarise Govt Buildings Mixed With Myriad Challenges
stories.title: India's Plan To Solarise Govt Buildings Mixed With Myriad Challenges
stories.summary: “Gujarat issues tender to solarise government buildings with rooftop solar.” Swap in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, or any of a dozen others, and the headline still reads true — India has been running an almost continuous rotation of state-level rooftop solar tenders for government buildings through 2026. Rajasthan’s RRECL floated 33 MW in January. REIL, a central PSU, tendered 17.5 MW spanning multiple states the same month. NHPC issued 16.64 MW for central ministry buildings in February and another tranche for Sikkim, Manipur and Nagaland in May. Uttarakhand’s UREDA followed with 6.5 MW in June, Maharashtra’s MEDA has been quietly tendering primary health centres district by district, and UP’s UPNEDA issued 11 MW just this week. Nearly all of them use the same template: RESCO mode, tariff-based competitive bidding, a 25-year power purchase agreement, and roughly nine months from signing to commissioning. What almost none of them come with is a follow-up. Tender notices are routine, well-publicised and easy to track. Completion data is not. The handful of disclosures that do exist, mostly forced out through legislative questions rather than volunteered in press releases suggest the gap between announcement and execution is wide, and wider in some states than others. THE NATIONAL NUMBER, THREE WEEKS OLD The clearest recent data point is a Lok Sabha answer from August 5, 2026. Responding to a question on rooftop solar mandates for government offices, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy disclosed that it had received Action Plans for solarising 41,972 Central Government buildings, of which 24,376 or about 58 percent had actually been solarised, adding up to roughly 854 MW. States and Union Territories, taken together, reported 81,754 government buildings solarised with a cumulative capacity of about 1,447 MW. Notably, the ministry could not or did not supply the denominator for the state figure, there is no total eligible-building count against which to measure that 81,754, which makes it impossible to compute a comparable completion rate for states the way the Centre’s own 58 percent can be computed. The same answer contained a smaller but telling admission: no Central Financial Assistance is available for rooftop solar on government buildings, because MNRE considers such installations “financially viable... even without CFA.” That assumption does a lot of work in explaining what follows. WHERE THE GRANULAR NUMBERS EXIST Karnataka is the one state that has put a hard number on the record recently, and it is stark. According to the state Energy Department, nearly 59,000 government buildings could together generate 698.2 MW of rooftop solar. As of this month, only 2,624 buildings — under 5 percent — have actually been fitted, totalling 33.68 MW, itself under 5 percent of the technical potential identified. A senior official acknowledged the shortfall directly, pointing to funding constraints and the absence of subsidy support for institutional buildings as the core blockers — essentially confirming, from the state side, the gap the Centre’s own no-CFA policy leaves open. Madhya Pradesh offers a useful before-and-after. In June 2025, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced that all government buildings in the state would carry rooftop solar by the end of 2025. That deadline has now passed with no completion announcement to match the original promise; the only recent capacity figure attached to Madhya Pradesh, 566 MW, refers to nearly 1.5 lakh residential PM Surya Ghar installations, not government buildings, and cannot be used as a proxy for the CM’s pledge. Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu occupy a middle position: MNRE has repeatedly named them as states “performing well” on government-building solarisation, most recently in a March 2025 ministry statement that also noted Chandigarh and Daman & Diu had reached full saturation of their government-building targets. But “performing well” is a qualitative label, not a disclosed percentage, and none of the four states appears to have published a Karnataka-style ratio of buildings solarised against buildings eligible. Gujarat’s own public figure — 2,451 government buildings solarised, from a 2024 state report — has no accompanying denominator either, so it is impossible to say from the public record whether Gujarat’s position as a stated leader reflects a genuinely higher completion rate or simply a larger base of early installations from a state that has run solar policy since 2009. WHY THE GAP EXISTS Three structural threads run through the disclosures that do exist. First, the financing assumption: MNRE’s position that government buildings don’t need Central Financial Assistance because RESCO tariffs are self-liquidating collides with the reality that RESCO payments still have to clear government budget-approval cycles, which move slower than a developer’s working-capital timeline. Second, net-metering and billing integration with DISCOMs remains a persistent friction point at the point of commissioning — an old but illustrative Himachal Pradesh case saw completed rooftop systems left non-functional for want of a working billing interface with the state board. Third, the CAG’s broader audit findings on renewable energy projects — including a specific finding that Coal India had covered only 4.08 percent of its 3,000 MW solar mandate by December 2024, with rooftop work orders issued for just 34.56 MW — point to a pattern of delay at every stage from planning through execution across public-sector renewable projects generally, not just rooftop-on-buildings specifically. None of this means the tenders are cosmetic. RESCO structures, competitive tariffs and 25-year PPAs are the correct mechanism, and the steady tender flow shows states are still actively working the pipeline rather than letting it lapse. What it does mean is that the tender is the visible, low-friction 10 percent of the process, and the commissioning, metering and reporting that follow are where the programme is actually tested — and where almost no state volunteers data unless a legislator forces the question. WHAT TO WATCH INSTEAD OF THE NEXT TENDER For anyone tracking this beyond the headline, the signal is not the next state to issue a tender — that is close to guaranteed to happen again within weeks. The signal is the next legislative answer or RTI response that discloses a completion number against a stated target, the way Karnataka’s assembly and the August 5 Lok Sabha reply did. Those are still rare enough that each one is worth a story in its own right, and collectively they are the only real audit trail this programme currently has.

article_sentences: A Delhi Court has convicted Sukesh Chandrashekhar for calling up a judicial officer who was presiding over a corruption case lodged against him, then impersonating a Supreme Court judge and pressurizing the trial judge to grant him bail further threatening the judicial officer with adverse professional ramifications if bail wasn't granted.

The allegation against Sukesh was that while in police custody in connection with a 2017 corruption case he obtained access to a constable's mobile phone in whose custody he was and thereafter used it to contact the official landline and mobile number of the judicial officer who was presiding over the corruption case.
"There are cases which test the law.
There are cases which test the evidence.
And then there are cases which test the limits of human audacity and mendacity.

The present case belongs, rather unfortunately, to the last category as it presents a particularly disturbing instance of an alleged attempt to interfere with the administration of justice by approaching a Judicial Officer through an extraordinary and wholly impermissible method..."

The court further noted that the accused allegedly tried to impersonate first as a Private Secretary of a then sitting Judge of the Supreme Court of India and later as the Judge himself and then sought to persuade the Judicial Officer to grant bail to the accused at the earliest.
"The impersonator did not allegedly present himself as an ordinary citizen.
He borrowed the highest judicial authority in the land.

The purpose was apparently to create an aura of unquestionable command, where he was not merely asking a Judicial Officer to grant bail to the accused but was using the authority of a Judge of the Highest Court of the Land, to browbeat the Judicial Officer.
He allegedly threatened her with adverse professional ramifications if the indulgence of bail was not extended to the accused," the court added.
The CJM said that the present case was qualitatively different from an ordinary case of cheating or impersonation.

stories.headline: India, China agree on eight measures to improve border management
stories.title: India, China agree on eight measures to improve border management
stories.summary: India and China have agreed on a series of measures to improve border management, maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) and advance negotiations for a settlement of the boundary question, following talks between National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing. The 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives (SRs) of India and China on the boundary question was held on August 25. Doval, India’s Special Representative, and Wang Yi, China’s Special Representative, held a “candid and in-depth” exchange of views and reached an eight-point consensus. Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas and creating conditions for the stable development of bilateral relations. They also agreed to advance negotiations on a framework for resolving the boundary dispute in line with the 2005 Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles and subsequent understandings reached during the SR talks. As part of the effort, the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and the Working Group on Border Management under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) will begin discussions on an “early and substantial harvest” on boundary delimitation and border management. Their first task will be to finalise their respective terms of reference. India and China also agreed that situations arising on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC and local commander-level meetings, to prevent misunderstandings and miscalculations along the LAC. The two sides agreed to establish two additional meeting points for General-Level Mechanism/Senior Highest Military Commander meetings. They also agreed on two additional channels for military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors to improve communication between the two militaries. Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, border trade The two sides noted progress in trans-border cooperation. India welcomed China’s decision to increase the number of batches of Indian pilgrims undertaking the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra in the Tibet Autonomous Region. Both sides also welcomed the reopening of three designated border trading points and agreed to strengthen cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas. They said the objective was to create an atmosphere of dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas. India and China further agreed to hold the next meeting of the Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and continue discussions on issues including hydrological data sharing and renewal of relevant memorandums of understanding. The two sides also decided that the 26th round of Special Representatives’ talks will be held in India in 2027.

The Bill proposes strict punishment for religious conversion allegedly carried out through force, coercion, undue influence, allurement, fraudulent means or marriage.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice to the Delhi.
Police in a bail plea filed by co-accused Athar Khan in the 2020 North-East Delhi riots "larger conspiracy" case.
A bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M Pancholi issued notice in a special leave petition filed by Khan challenging the Delhi High Court's July 7 order denying him bail.
He was also denied bail by the Trial Court.
Athar Khan has sought bail on grounds of parity with Shadab Ahmad, who was granted bail by the Supreme Court in January 2026.

Khan was arrested in FIR No. 59/2020 under Sections 13/16/17/18 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967; Sections 302/307/353/186/212/395/ 427/435/436/452/454/109/114/147/148/124A/153A/120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

It may be noted that a bench comprising Justice Kumar and Justice PB Varale has referred to a larger bench the question of understanding the 3-judge bench judgment in Union of India v KA Najeeb(2021), which held that long incarceration can be a ground to grant bail in cases under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act, regardless of the statutory rigours.
The reference was made while granting interim bail to co-accused Tasleem Ahmed and Khalid Saifi.

The reference came as a consequence to a judgment delivered by a two-judge bench(Justices BV Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan) in Syed Ifthikar Andrabi, which criticised the judgments in Gulfisha Fatima and Gurwinder Singh (both authored by Justice Aravind Kumar), saying that they took a narrow view regarding bail in UAPA cases.
The bench in Andrabi took the view that Gulfisha Fatima and Gurwinder Singh departed from the KA Najeeb verdict.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Seeks CBI Response On Sandip Ghosh's Bail Plea In RG Kar Medical Hospital Case
stories.title: Supreme Court Seeks CBI Response On Sandip Ghosh's Bail Plea In RG Kar Medical Hospital Case
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation(CBI) on a bail plea filed by former principal of R G Kar Hospital Sandip Ghosh, accused of financial irregularities and corruption.
A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale has sought CBI's response by October 15.
Ghosh was the Principal of the Hospital and College where the brutal rape and murder of a junior doctor took place on August 9, 2024.
The High Court on August 13, 2024, had transferred the investigation to the CBI relating to the doctor's death.
He was initially called in for questioning by the CBI, which later arrested him on charges of financial irregularities at the hospital, followed by his alleged role in the aftermath of the incident.
Nationwide protests broke out, leading to the Supreme Court taking suo motu cognisance of the same.

Ghosh had also moved the Supreme Court challenging the Calcutta High Court's order to transfer the SIT probe into alleged irregularities in the tender processes and mismanagement by Ghosh, to the CBI.
The Court had declined to entertain his plea.

The allegation against Ghosh was levelled by former Deputy Superintendent at RG Kar, Akhtar Ali, who moved the Calcutta High Court against former principal Dr Ghosh, alleging serious illegalities committed by the former principal.
In his plea, Ali alleged that Ghosh committed serious illegalities, such as mismanagement of dead bodies, reselling biowaste in the open market, misutilization of public funds etc.
Ghosh has been granted bail in the case alleging a cover-up in the brutal rape and murder case after the CBI failed to file its chargesheet within the stipulated time of 90 days.
However, he remains in CBI custody in the financial irregularities matter.
